entries.title: Band 6 of the official training_features.tif is a radiometric band mis-tagged as magnetic
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 carries data_category='magnetic_data' and description='Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection' in the organiser's own file. It is the GeoDAWN aeroradiometric total-count (TC) grid. src/gems52/features.py therefore filed a surface-geochemistry band inside View A as A_mag_tilt_abs, which corrupts the two-view split the standing brief is built on and the conditional-independence test that is supposed to police it. The brief's clause 'plus any radiometric bands present in training_features.tif' resolves to one band, not to none.
entries.how_we_know: Measured on the bytes, 150,000-pixel sample: Spearman(band6, GeoDAWN TC grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band6, K+Th+U) = +0.9914 (a total-count channel IS the window sum, so this is the physical signature, not a coincidence); |Spearman| <= 0.149 against all five magnetic bands in the same file (TMI -0.0250, TMI up-continued 150 m +0.0079, TMI horizontal gradient -0.1489, TMI vertical gradient +0.0214, RTP -0.0914). A magnetic-field derivative cannot be uncorrelated with the magnetic field. Band 6 is also strictly positive (min 2.953, max 88.573) while a tilt angle is bounded by +/- pi/2. Official source for the TC grid: Glen & Earney 2024, USGS data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93LGLVQ.
entries.disposition: corrected - src/gems55/radlayers.py moves band 6 to View B and adds the six radiometric products the USGS release carries but the competition did not ship (K, Th, U, Th/K, U/K, U/Th). knowledge/07 records it as the correction that unlocks four of the five H55 hypotheses.

entries.title: The README states the grid as '3730 x 3292', which is height x width
entries.what_it_is: rasterio reports width=3292, height=3730 for every official raster; grid.SHAPE = (3730, 3292) is (rows, cols). Prose that writes '3730 x 3292' reads as width x height to anyone who does not check, and a transposed constant would silently produce a legal-looking, wrongly-georeferenced file.

entries.title: |G| is not published, but it is recoverable from the metric and our own scored history
entries.what_it_is: The number of hidden public-test truth pixels drives the credit bar and therefore the file size, and the organiser does not publish it. knowledge/05 fixed the budget at K=37654 'to match the 0.2778 file's footprint mass', i.e. inherited it from an unrelated submission rather than deriving it.
entries.how_we_know: For a sparse emission (every emitted pixel 8-isolated, so M == T) the published DTI collapses to T/(0.2*S + 0.8*|G|) with one unknown; T <= |G| then gives |G| >= 0.2*DTI*S/(1 - 0.8*DTI) per submission. Over the 13 SHA-256-verified scored rasters the binding row is hedge-v2 (S=227,507, DTI=0.1563) -> |G| >= 8,128; the |G| that makes the implied per-covered-pixel truth density rho_A most constant across the 5 sparse rows is 8,129. knowledge/01's independent loss decomposition of the 0.2778 file gave 8,000 (tax 6,757 / credit 3,870 / miss 3,304), i.e. two different derivations agree to 1.6 %.
entries.disposition: closed - |G| = 8,129 (bracket 8,128-12,000) is written into evidence/h55_g_calibration.json and is the number the H55 credit bar uses. Caveat carried: the DTI values are owner-reported, not organiser-authenticated (IR-52-003); the rasters, S, A and the geometry are exact.

entries.title: The family's best submission spends only 86% of the kernel's placement efficiency
entries.what_it_is: One isolated emitted pixel can contribute at most 9.380298 of kernel-weighted coverage A (the disc weight sum, enumerated exactly). A/S = 8.044 for the 0.2778 file (86% of the ceiling), 7.956 for d2-8, 6.564 for d1-5, 3.813-3.937 for the contiguous h19/h16 files (41%), 1.664 for the placeholder (18%). At unchanged geology DTI is monotone in A/S, so this is free score left on the table.
entries.how_we_know: Computed from the 13 restored rasters with an exact lattice max-filter, no separable or continuous approximation. Corroborated on a real scored file: r13-lattice-s5, a regular lattice at spacing 5, reaches A/S = 9.361 = 99.8% of the ceiling. Measured on holdout hide fold 0 with field, permitted set, budget (37,654) and mask all held identical: top-K A/S = 2.233 -> DTI 0.03196; hard-core 400 m A/S = 8.76 -> DTI 0.10101; matched random A/S ~ 9.38 -> DTI 0.04291.
entries.disposition: open - src/gems55/emit_opt.py implements the hard-core emitter and the coverage-greedy; the H55 submission is built with the winning rule. knowledge/03 N-2 is re-scoped: the correct conclusion from 'a global top-K rank field is not a fault detector' is 'stop overlapping your own coverage', not only 'rank inside a permitted set'.

entries.title: Our own coverage-greedy wrote its running cover into a throwaway copy, and a test caught it
entries.what_it_is: src/gems55/emit_opt.py updated its running cover with `np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk, out=cf[nbi])`. Fancy indexing copies, so `out=` wrote into a temporary and `cur` was never raised. Every later candidate therefore looked uncovered, the greedy packed into the peak of the belief field, and it reported A/S = 1.8-2.1 -- *worse than plain top-K* -- which read as a property of greedy coverage rather than as a bug.
entries.how_we_know: tests/test_h53_emit.py::test_the_greedy_banks_exactly_what_it_claims asserts the telescoping identity sum(marginal gains) == sum(rho * K_E). It failed at 107.7 vs 66.6 on a 140x140 grid. After the one-line fix the greedy reaches A/S = 9.27 (98.8% of the 9.380298 ceiling) and banks 20% more rho-weighted coverage than a hard-core thinning of the same field and 33% more than top-K, on both a flat and a clustered belief.
entries.disposition: fixed - `cf[nbi] = np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk)`. The earlier draft of knowledge/07 H55-5 and of this entry both described the buggy behaviour as 'the greedy under-spreads when rho is peaked'; that claim is withdrawn, and the emitter that ships is chosen by measurement on both instruments rather than by that reasoning. Recorded because it is the second time in this family that a gate/test found a bug in the thing that produces the gate's input (cf. IR-52-007).

entries.title: The organiser's band-6 tag is contradicted by the survey contractor's own read-me: band 6 is radiometric total count, and the competition grid is node-aligned to the survey grid
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 of data/training_features.tif is tagged data_category = magnetic_data, 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection'. The GeoDAWN contractor read-me (NV5 / EDCON-PRJ, December 2022, Task Order 140G0221F0024) lists tc_raw and tccorr under Radiometrics and contains no tilt-angle channel anywhere in its channel inventory, so the tag does not correspond to any product the survey delivered. The same document gives the survey's Area 2 origin as 243200.0 / 4135400.0 at 100 m spacing, which is node-aligned to the competition grid rather than pixel-aligned.
entries.how_we_know: Two independent lines. First, the contractor read-me's own channel inventory. Second, measured on the bytes: Spearman(band 6, GeoDAWN total-count grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band 6, K+Th+U) = +0.9915, which is what a total-count channel is by construction; and |Spearman| <= 0.148 against all five magnetic bands in the same file. Band 6 is also strictly positive (range 2.953 to 88.573), where a tilt angle is bounded by +/-pi/2. Independently corroborated by IR-52-019.
entries.handling: Band 6 is assigned to View B (as B_band6_TC), not to the potential-field view. A radiometric band inside View A would corrupt the conditional-independence test the two views are required to pass. Enforced by tests/test_r4.py::test_band6_is_in_view_b.

The arm is ABANDONED as a scored candidate.

entries.title: The prior family's per-cell credit allocation is under-determined; only an interval is knowable (credited-core alternate round)
entries.what_it_is: Thirteen owner-reported scores plus the |G| = 14,088.7 px anchor identify the family's total credit but not its per-cell allocation: 574 coverage patterns vs 13 equations. A linear program gives the honest interval for the 25,517-cell credited core: [4,079.1, 5,249.2] px of credit (0.5 % slack on the 4-decimal reported scores). Adding 'more detectors agreeing implies not-less credit' makes the system INFEASIBLE — the reported scores contradict that monotone-consensus model.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_credit_lp2.json, evidence/gems57_credit_robust.json, work/credit_lp.py (the coarser coverage-count model is also infeasible, same reason); scipy HiGHS linprog.
entries.disposition: Every projection in the README/site/knowledge is published as a bracket (0.227-0.336 for the shipped file), not as a point forecast. The pair identity T(ref) = T(d2-8) = 5,223.13 is still exact and is what pins the anchor.

entries.title: Three instrument defects produced confident wrong answers before they were caught
entries.observation: (1) Layers.matrix reshaped a layer-major memmap into a (layers*rows, cols) matrix; scikit-learn accepted it and reported 3,292 features instead of 39. (2) make_folds buffered on the component fold id, which is -1 off-catalogue, marking the whole grid as boundary and leaving 0 catalogue pixels in training on every fold. (3) The arm's legal set ANDed the catalogue visibility mask into the grid, restricting every arm to still-mapped faults; all arms then scored exactly 0.0000.
entries.handling: All three fixed in src/gems52/h57.py with a regression test for each the axis convention in particular, which had none.

entries.disposition: fixed
entries.title: The hide-and-recover survival check contradicted itself, and the first fold assignment emptied the training positives

entries.title: The lane-drift 3 px proximity component uses a 25-cell L1 diamond, not the metric's 29-cell Euclidean disc
entries.what_it_is: h60d.lane_drift_report measures 'dots within 3 px' with scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation(prior_dots, iterations=3), whose default structure is the 4-connected cross. Three iterations therefore produce the 25-cell L1 diamond, whereas the competition metric's kernel k(d) = max(1 - d/R, 0) with R = 3 px covers the 29-cell Euclidean disc. Every near-dot fraction this repository has reported is consequently a LOWER bound on the fraction of dots within the metric's own 300 m acceptance radius.
entries.how_we_know: Measured: the dilation of a single pixel on a 20x20 grid covers 25 of 400 cells, not 29; pinned by tests/test_h62.py::test_revealed_colocation_matches_a_hand_computation. The metric's disc is enumerated by gems52.metric._offsets (29 offsets at |offset| <= 3 px).
entries.disposition: Disclosed rather than silently widened: changing the structure now would make every prior round's proximity number unverifiable, and the reading is conservative in the direction that matters (a run that passes at 0.2781 on the diamond would read higher on the disc, so the gate is not being made easier to pass without saying so). H61's worst gate value is 0.2781 against a 0.70 bar, so theconclusion does not change under the wider disc.

entries.what_it_is: The statistic 'fraction of YOUR dots within 3 px of prior P' has chance level equal to P's own 3 px coverage of the eligible footprint: a uniformly random emission lands inside P's halo with exactly that probability. The rule's trigger is 0.70, so for any prior whose coverage is at or above 0.70 the rule fires on a random emission and cannot indicate lane drift. Measured over the 545-raster registry: 14 rasters have coverage >= 0.95 (probes under the preregistered policy) and 31 have coverage >= 0.70; of the 23 near-offenders, 14 are probes and all 9 informative ones have coverage 0.7583-0.8976 with NEGATIVE excess over chance (-0.0054 to -0.0291). Across all 545 priors the median excess is -0.0766 and only 108 are positive, i.e. the H61 emission is less clustered near prior dots than uniform chance. Max Spearman is 0.0361 (literal) / 0.0209 (policy) against a 0.90 trigger.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h61_lane_analysis.py over evidence/h61_lane_dots.json (gems52.gates.lane_report on the written artefact, 545 rasters, 361 distinct decoded patterns), which itself measured per-prior coverage with gems52.gates.registry_coverage.
entries.handling: The preregistered probe threshold (0.95) and the literal 0.70/3 px rule were NOT relaxed: the recorded verdict stays DUPLICATE/STOP and the artefact stays research-only. The chance-normalised excess is published beside it so the reader can see that the STOP is a property of the registry's geometry, not evidence of a copied lane.
entries.disposition: Prospective fix for the shared selector, to adopt BEFORE the next round: apply the directed proximity rule only to priors whose measured coverage is below the rule's own trigger, or test the chance-normalised excess (near - coverage) against a margin. Both forms follow from the rule rather than being tuned to a result.

entries.title: This round preregistered its emission budget on a |G| bracket that is disjoint from the measured one
entries.status: open - disclosed as correction H62-4; the emission was not changed
entries.what_it_is: registry/h62_preregistration.json derives the 22,000 px emission budget from the champion-family decay gamma = 0.2284 evaluated over a |G| bracket of 18,000-19,300 px, which yields S* = 21,300-22,870 px. That bracket is DISJOINT from the interval |G| is actually identified to live in. |G| is bounded below by T <= |G| applied to the largest off-catalogue support (calib_8GEMSDOE_Hedge-v2, 166,519 px at score 0.1563 -> |G| >= 5,949.3 px) and above by monotone credit on the tightest nested scored pair (d15 60,069 px subset gems27_tgc_v2_d15 61,328 px, 0.2477 > 0.2449 -> |G| <= 12,512.1 px). The legacy point |G| = 14,088.7 px used by knowledge/10 and carried into this round is a valid but NON-BINDING upper bound (it comes from the weaker nested pair h33-2-b2 subset d28); treating it as a point value additionally assumes the champion's 6,436 deleted ring pixels earn exactly zero credit, and it falls to 7,066 px if they earn 100 px.
entries.how_we_know: Independently re-derived in this checkout: the subset relation d15 subset gems27 and the 166,519 px off-catalogue support were recomputed from the manifest-pinned bytes directly, and both bounds reproduce evidence/h61_forensics.json (main's H61) to four decimal places. The nested-pair algebra is G <= 0.25*(s_y*S_y - s_x*S_x)/(s_x - s_y) from DTI = T/(0.2 S + 0.8|G|) with T monotone in support; the lower-bound algebra is G >= 0.2*s*S/(1 - 0.8*s) from T <= |G|. Recorded in the build receipt as g_bracket_px and g_sensitivity.
entries.disposition: Disclosed as correction H62-4 rather than silently re-emitting. Under the measured bracket the two available gamma rules disagree: this round's own gamma = 0.6453 clamps S* to 30,000 px at every |G| in the bracket, while the champion-family gamma = 0.2284 gives S* = 7,044-14,815 px and clamps to 15,000 px. The direct board measurement - score strictly decreasing in emitted mass across the six off-catalogue scored priors (Spearman -1.000, n = 6) - breaks the tie toward the LOW end, so 15,000 px is the value the evidence favours and 22,000 px is above it. The shipped file is left at 22,000 px (the preregistered fallback, which sits between the two model answers) rather than churned a second time after the review; the budget is now the weakest link in this round and is the first item for the next session.

entries.title: Marginal bar: the metric's special case gives α·DTI (0.0556 at 0.2778); the repository's accept_bar gives α·DTI/(1−α·DTI) (0.0588)
entries.what_it_is: Metric identity (ii) in src/gems52/metric.py: an addition helps iff c·(1−α·DTI) > α·DTI·f, with c the credit increment and f the false-positive increment. For one uncovered truth pixel with kernel weight w (f = 1−w) this gives w > α·DTI = 0.0556 at DTI 0.2778. emit.accept_bar(dti) = α·DTI/(1−α·DTI) = 0.0588 is the f = 1 form, which is stricter. README's ≈0.055 is the special case, rounded. An earlier H66 draft called 0.0588 the marginal bar; that draft was wrong.
entries.how_we_know: Algebra from metric identities (i) and (ii), and direct evaluation of emit.accept_bar at DTI 0.2778 (this session).

entries.disposition: Open, low. Decide in a future round whether emit.accept_bar should use the special-case form; the current form is more conservative than the metric's marginal condition.
